video.title: When You Get A Low Forehand

classification.reason: The coach gives an actionable cue to tilt the torso and let the chest almost face the ground when preparing for a low forehand.

problem.title_as_question: How should you adjust your body when dealing with a low forehand?
problem.definition: On a low forehand, players struggle to strike the ball with their normal swing mechanics if they do not tilt their torso.

quotes.text: When you get a low forehand, tilt your torso.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: That'll let you strike the ball the way you normally do.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: If the ball is sufficiently low, your chest can almost be facing the ground as you prepare.
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: The incoming ball is low to the ground, requiring an adjustment to strike normally.

causes.statement: Failing to tilt the torso on a low ball prevents you from striking the ball the way you normally do.

angles.summary: Tilting the torso allows you to maintain your normal striking mechanics even when the ball is low.
On sufficiently low balls, the chest can be almost facing the ground as you prepare.

solutions.summary: When you get a low forehand, tilt your torso so your chest can almost face the ground during preparation.
